From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 14:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Safety questionnaire + evidence for misuse monitoring

Mina / Neha —

Draft of the technical evidence is attached. Highlights:

- Misuse detection: we operate an online rule + model hybrid. Rules detect high-confidence policy violations (regex + heuristics) and are complemented by an ML classifier that flags low-confidence but high-risk prompts for human review.
- Alerting: alerts are routed to PagerDuty + Slack channel #sec-abuse; critical alerts generate an automated incident in our internal tracking system with initial triage metadata. Example alert rule included in the spreadsheet.
- Logging / retention: request and response metadata (non-sensitive headers and model identifiers) are retained for 90 days by default for misuse monitoring; customers can opt into longer retention for dedicated/private deployments. Payloads are redacted by default (no customer PII stored in audit logs).
- Evidence: "logs_sample_augmented.txt" is a syntheticized snippet that mirrors the fields we retain (timestamp, route, model_version, policy_tags, alert_score, reviewer_id). See the sample alert line and note about hash-based user tokenization.

Attached: misuse_monitoring_playbook.xlsx; logs_sample_augmented.txt

Quick note on metrics we provide: per-route abuse-rate, false positive/false negative tracking on labeled review sets, time-to-first-response for human review. We can include a short export from our internal dashboard showing an example timeline if they want.

Dev
Product Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: misuse_monitoring_playbook.xlsx (spreadsheet), logs_sample_augmented.txt (text)

Hi Jamie —

Please find attached our completed questionnaire (redwood_rfi_answer_document_v1.pdf). I’ve annotated answers where we reference supporting artifacts and included inline links to the playbook and logs sample. Key clarifications we added:

- Incident notification: Redwood supports configurable SLAs; for hosted customers we default to 24-hour acknowledgement for critical misuse incidents and a 72-hour remediation window for triageable content. We included the trigger logic for automated escalation.
- Data handling: payloads are redacted at ingestion; we include a hash-based user token to support investigation without exposing PII.
- Third-party attestations: SOC 2 Type II certificate is in our compliance package — we referenced the artifacts and offered to provide redacted audit excerpts under NDA.

Procurement — we’re on track to deliver the full package and can provide a Docusign-enabled statement of evidence if that helps for record-keeping.

Neha Kapoor
